quotes.text: Learn how to set up your integration with Amazon Pay.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: If you don’t want to use dynamic payment methods, follow the steps below to manually configure the payment methods in your Checkout integration.

If no action is taken after 10 minutes, the [PaymentMethod](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/object.md) is detached and the [PaymentIntent](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/object.md) object’s status automatically transitions to `requires_payment_method`.

Stripe cancels the PaymentIntent and sends a [payment_intent.canceled](https://docs.stripe.com/api/events/types.md#event_types-payment_intent.canceled) event if the payment isn’t captured during the 7-day window.
You can create Amazon Pay payments in any of the supported currencies, regardless of the country your business operates in with the exception of the US.

findings: Semantic raw delta is navigation-only: the November capture has a shared purpose line and five variant routes for Checkout, Elements, Direct API, iOS and Android (new raw lines 5-18), while the diff removes the detailed May body in favor of the index (diff lines 1-19, 1380-1387). It proves no current change to Amazon Pay behavior, compatibility, SDK requirements, or payment outcomes.

The mapped source already summarizes the five old variants and retains May raw provenance (source lines 4-8, 11-35). Add the November raw as navigation-only provenance without replacing or redating May functionality; the current source does not yet route to the new index (source lines 6-7, 33-35; new raw lines 9-18).

Independent baseline precision issue: the source states a general 10-minute authorization window (source lines 13, 21), but the old Elements section limits the 10-minute action deadline to a PaymentIntent in requires_action after redirect to Amazon; decline or timeout detaches the PaymentMethod and returns the Intent to requires_payment_method (old raw lines 679-685). The 7-day window is a separate manual-capture deadline after successful authorization, ending in cancellation if uncaptured (old raw lines 613-649; source line 23).

Checkout's explicit payment_method_types example belongs to the manual-configuration route; the older guide first offers dynamic payment methods and says manual configuration is for those who do not use dynamic methods (old raw lines 12-16, 33-39). Source line 19 should retain this choice rather than implying amazon_pay must always be manually listed.

The baseline currency contradiction remains unresolved: the old Elements error table says Amazon Pay only supports usd (old raw lines 687-696), whereas its own Direct API supported-currencies table lists 12 currencies (old raw lines 886-892), also matching the separate May overview (raw/stripe-amazon-pay-2025.md lines 20-22, 136-142). Source lines 13 and 29 identify the conflict but call it a 'likely doc error'; that inference should be framed as unresolved, not a verified correction.

For web and mobile variants, the older capture distinguishes server-created Checkout Session or PaymentIntent, client secret and client confirmation/redirect, subsequent Intent status or payment_intent.succeeded event, and testing versus live flows (old raw lines 35-90, 127-175, 394-499, 607-685, 717-864, 991-1148, 1234-1381). A return URL, client callback or created Intent alone does not prove payment success or capture.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain the May 7, 2026 five-variant routing and the distinct Checkout hosted/embedded Session examples, Elements and Direct API PaymentIntent examples, iOS STPPaymentHandler and Android PaymentLauncher examples as dated only (old raw lines 8-110, 127-171, 698-730, 894-900, 1105-1142, 1162-1168, 1306-1353).

Retain the conditional requires_action 10-minute Amazon redirect deadline and requires_payment_method fallback, separate 7-day manual-capture requires_capture/canceled boundary, and event/status verification rather than browser return alone (old raw lines 490-544, 607-659, 679-685).

Retain May currency contradiction, not an unqualified USD-only rule or a verified 12-currency promise for all merchants; old raw lines 687-696 conflict with 886-892 and the separate May overview raw/stripe-amazon-pay-2025.md lines 136-142.

Preserve May-specific platform/setup examples: Elements Stripe.js script and HTTPS live-page guidance (old raw lines 244-264), iOS 13+ SDK claim and webview callback setup (old raw lines 917-989, 1063-1107), Android sample dependency 23.7.0 and PaymentLauncher flow (old raw lines 1185-1230, 1306-1353); none is renewed by November navigation.
conflicts: The old same-URL source's Elements error table says USD only while its Direct API table lists twelve currencies (old raw lines 687-696, 886-892); a separate May overview also lists twelve (raw/stripe-amazon-pay-2025.md lines 20-22, 136-142). Keep a reciprocal warning and do not resolve eligibility from an unread November variant (new raw lines 13-18; source lines 13, 29).

The source's broad '10-minute authorization window' wording (source lines 13, 21) can conflate the requires_action customer step with the distinct 7-day post-authorization manual-capture deadline (old raw lines 613-649, 679-685).
The source's Checkout method-type shorthand (source line 19) omits the dynamic-method alternative and could be mistaken for a universal prerequisite (old raw lines 12-16, 33-39).
unresolved_questions: The five November variant bodies were not in the pinned packet and were not fetched; present-day eligibility, currency support, mobile SDK versions, and whether the old USD-only error text persists cannot be established from new raw lines 9-18.

findings: Add November index provenance with navigation-only labeling (source lines 6-7, 33-35; new raw lines 9-18). Narrow 10 minutes to the requires_action step after Amazon redirect and keep it separate from seven-day manual capture (source lines 13, 21-23; old raw lines 613-649, 679-685). Qualify manual payment_method_types as a choice alongside dynamic methods (source line 19; old raw lines 12-16, 33-39).
conflicts: Retain, but label unresolved, the old USD-only error text versus twelve-currency tables; 'likely a doc error' in source line 29 is an inference, and November supplies no current currency body (old raw lines 687-696, 886-892; new raw lines 9-18).
source_assessments.reason: The new capture contributes variant navigation only, but the existing summary needs bounded provenance and baseline-accuracy corrections.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/amazon-pay/accept-a-payment, the full November capture establishes only an Amazon Pay integration purpose and routes to Checkout, Elements, Direct API, iOS and Android variants (new raw lines 5-18); it does not itself state their prerequisites or confirm any transaction. The May capture describes a Checkout Session with same-currency line items and dynamic or manually selected methods, versus server-created PaymentIntents handed to web/mobile clients for Amazon authentication and status verification (old raw lines 12-39, 127-175, 490-544, 717-864, 991-1148, 1234-1381). The mapped source-stripe-amazon-pay-accept-payment.md covers these paths (source lines 11-27), but its 10-minute wording needs the requires_action condition and its Checkout shorthand needs the dynamic-method alternative; manual capture has a separate seven-day deadline (old raw lines 613-649, 679-685).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/amazon-pay/accept-a-payment, the November index is a presentation and navigation change, with no demonstrated substantive behavior change (new raw lines 9-18; old raw lines 8-18, 894-900, 1162-1168). In source-stripe-amazon-pay-accept-payment.md, retain May-only Checkout, Elements, Direct API and mobile instructions as dated, including server/client separation, requires_action timeout, requires_capture manual-capture window, and success-event or PaymentIntent-status checks (source lines 11-35; old raw lines 490-544, 613-659, 679-685). The old USD-only error text conflicts with its twelve-currency table and separate May overview, so its 'likely doc error' label is inference rather than resolution (old raw lines 687-696, 886-892; raw/stripe-amazon-pay-2025.md lines 136-142). Neither redirect nor November route proves payment success, capture, currency eligibility, or current iOS/Android SDK behavior.
